reviews.title: Decent, but Email Guard misses most scam emails
reviews.text:
I recently subscribed to a multi-device Premium Security plan.

After a first week of frustration in which Avast wasn't recognizing my Premium plan on iPhone or iPad, Avast fixed it after a call to customer support that got escalated to Tier 2 support.

The Avast feature I care most about is Scam Guardian using AI. To test the effectiveness of this feature, I connected Email Guard to an old account that receives lots of spam and scam emails. Email Guard has caught a few, but misses most, scam emails.

A telltale sign that an email is fraudulent is that it fails SPF, DKIM, or DMARC. Even after failing one of these obvious authentication protocols, Email Guard and Mail Shield usually can't tell that an email is fraudulent.

If Email Guard and Mail Shield aren't checking the widely-used SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication protocols for email, then Call Guard probably isn't checking the USA-mandatory STIR/SHAKEN authentication protocol for phones calls.

Checking SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and STIR/SHAKEN is the easy stuff that any scam-detection software should be doing.

I have a 1-year subscription to Avast Premium Security, but if Scam Guardian doesn't greatly improve its effectiveness then I probably won't renew my subscription.

reviews.title: Buggy since the recent update, VPN disrupts my WiFi connection on my Apple devices (iPhone, iPad)

The WiFi symbol is still in the right corner, so it’s not switching to data, but apps and websites aren’t loading. When I switch the VPN off, I suddenly have my WiFi connection back.
My devices all have the most recent iOS, I’ve tried restarting them, I’ve deleted the Avast app and reinstalled, I’ve even reset my router network settings. I’m still encountering the problem. This is the first time this has happened in all the years I’ve been using Avast. And it’s only been happening since the last Avast update.
